instructions: Bihar STET Paper 2 Computer Science practice mock test.

questions.question: If `p` points to an element of an int array, `p+1` points to:

options.text: The next int element, advancing by sizeof(int) bytes
The next byte in all cases
The end of the whole program

questions.explanation: Pointer arithmetic advances by the size of the pointed-to type.

questions.question: The Observer pattern is commonly used to:

options.text: Notify dependent objects when a subject's state changes
Create exactly one instance of every class

questions.explanation: Observer defines a one-to-many dependency for state-change notifications.

questions.question: Round-robin scheduling is particularly characterized by:

options.text: Selection only by shortest total burst time
Permanent priority for the oldest process

questions.explanation: Each ready process receives a time slice in turn.

questions.question: A LEFT OUTER JOIN retains:

options.text: Only matching rows from both relations
All rows from the left relation, with matching right-side data where available
All rows from the right relation only
Only rows with NULL in both relations

questions.explanation: Unmatched left-side rows remain and right-side columns are filled with NULL.

questions.question: A topological ordering exists only for a:
questions.explanation: A DAG admits a linear order respecting every directed edge.

questions.question: Belady's anomaly is classically associated with which algorithm?
questions.explanation: FIFO can exhibit more page faults after adding frames in some reference strings.

questions.question: The main purpose of selecting a teaching aid is to:

options.text: Make the intended concept clearer and support the learning objective
Decorate the classroom regardless of content
Replace the need for a lesson objective
Increase the number of pages in notes

questions.explanation: Teaching aids should serve learning, not merely decoration.

questions.question: Gender-sensitive classroom practice includes:

options.text: Distributing opportunities and expectations without gender stereotypes
Assigning technical tasks only to boys
Asking only girls to maintain classroom cleanliness
Using gender as the sole basis for ability grouping

questions.explanation: Equitable practice challenges stereotypes and supports participation by all learners.

questions.question: If a teacher is unsure whether a resource is suitable for class, the teacher should:

options.text: Review its accuracy, age-appropriateness and alignment before use
Use it without checking because it is popular
Share it immediately with every student
Assume all online content is reliable

questions.explanation: Professional responsibility includes checking relevance, accuracy and suitability.

questions.question: What does `[x*x for x in range(3)]` produce?
questions.explanation: range(3) yields 0, 1, 2, whose squares are 0, 1, 4.

questions.question: A `private` member of a Java class is directly accessible:

options.text: Only within its declaring top-level class context, subject to nested-class rules
From every subclass regardless of package
From all objects of all classes

questions.explanation: Private access is restricted to the enclosing top-level class and its nested types under Java access rules.

questions.question: Which Java collection interface represents an ordered sequence that can contain duplicate elements?
questions.explanation: List is an ordered collection and permits duplicates.

questions.question: A reasonable accommodation is intended to:

options.text: Remove an access barrier without unnecessarily changing the essential learning outcome
Exempt every learner from all assessments

questions.explanation: Accommodations support equitable access while preserving essential requirements where possible.

questions.question: The sampling rate of digital audio indicates:

options.text: Number of samples captured per second
Length of the audio file in seconds

questions.explanation: Sampling rate is measured in samples per second, often Hz.

questions.question: The lower house of the Indian Parliament is the:
questions.explanation: Lok Sabha is the House of the People and the lower house.

questions.question: Kruskal's algorithm chooses edges in increasing weight order while avoiding:
questions.explanation: Kruskal adds the next lightest edge that does not form a cycle.

questions.question: Risk exposure is often estimated using:
questions.explanation: A common qualitative/quantitative approach combines likelihood and consequence.

questions.question: In a direct-mapped cache, a main-memory block can map to:

options.text: Any two lines selected by the OS

questions.explanation: Each memory block has a single possible cache-line location in direct mapping.

questions.question: A system call is an interface through which a program requests:

options.text: A service from the operating-system kernel

questions.explanation: System calls provide controlled access to kernel services.

questions.question: By De Morgan's law, (A·B)' is equivalent to:
questions.explanation: The complement of a product equals the sum of the complements.

questions.question: If a program takes 12 seconds on one processor and 6 seconds on another for the same workload, the speedup is:
questions.explanation: Speedup = old execution time / new execution time = 12/6 = 2.

questions.question: The Preamble describes India as a:
questions.explanation: These terms appear in the Preamble of the Constitution of India.

questions.question: An abstract data type primarily specifies:

options.text: The behavior and operations of a data type, not its implementation details
Only the physical memory address of every item

questions.explanation: An ADT describes operations and semantics independently of implementation.

questions.question: Which character terminates a C string?
questions.explanation: C strings are character sequences terminated by a null character.

questions.question: Clear classroom instructions should generally be:

options.text: Concise, sequenced and checked for understanding
Long, ambiguous and delivered only once
Different for each learner without reason

questions.explanation: Concise sequencing and comprehension checks support task completion.

questions.question: For a nonnegative integer x, `x & 1` is useful to test whether x is:
questions.explanation: The least significant bit is 1 for odd integers.

questions.question: A teacher reviewing lesson outcomes should use the evidence to:

options.text: Prove that every lesson must be identical
Replace learning objectives with marks only

questions.explanation: Reflection uses evidence to improve instruction.

questions.question: Atomicity means a transaction is:

options.text: Visible before commit to every transaction

questions.explanation: Atomicity prevents partial transaction effects from being committed as a completed transaction.

questions.question: The worst-case time complexity of quicksort is:
questions.explanation: Highly unbalanced partitions can yield quadratic time.

questions.question: Open educational resources are learning materials that are:

options.text: Available under an open licence or otherwise openly permitted for reuse and adaptation
Always copyrighted with no reuse permitted
Guaranteed to be factually correct without review

questions.explanation: OER licensing permits specified forms of access, reuse and adaptation.

questions.question: A major risk of function-like macros is that arguments may be:

options.text: Evaluated more than once after textual substitution

questions.explanation: Macro expansion can repeat argument expressions and cause unintended side effects.

questions.question: Header guards are primarily intended to prevent:

options.text: Repeated inclusion of the same header within a translation unit

questions.explanation: Include guards prevent repeated processing of a header's contents.

questions.question: A lexical analyzer typically groups characters into:
questions.explanation: Lexical analysis converts character streams into tokens.

questions.question: A probing question is used mainly to:

options.text: Encourage a learner to explain or clarify an initial answer

questions.explanation: Probing questions elicit deeper reasoning and clarification.

questions.question: A variable declared inside a block normally has which scope?
questions.explanation: A block-scope identifier is visible from its declaration to the end of its block, subject to rules.

questions.question: Tailgating in physical security means:

options.text: Following an authorized person into a restricted area without proper authorization
Sending too many packets to a server
Reading a file in reverse order

questions.explanation: Tailgating exploits physical access controls by following another person through a secured entry.

questions.question: A context switch involves:

options.text: Saving and restoring execution state between tasks

questions.explanation: The OS saves one task's state and restores another's.

questions.question: Statement: All roses are flowers. Which conclusion follows?
questions.explanation: The conclusion repeats the given universal statement.

questions.question: Backtracking algorithms typically:

options.text: Explore choices and abandon partial solutions that cannot lead to a valid result
Always examine every possible solution without pruning
Require all edge weights to be positive

questions.explanation: Backtracking prunes a search branch when it cannot yield a valid solution.

questions.question: Edge computing moves processing closer to:

options.text: A distant central data center in every case

questions.explanation: Edge processing can reduce latency and bandwidth needs.

questions.question: Java generics primarily provide:

options.text: Compile-time type safety for parameterized types
Automatic memory deallocation at a fixed time

questions.explanation: Generics catch many type mismatches at compile time and reduce casts.

questions.question: A device driver primarily acts as:

options.text: A translator between an OS and a hardware device
A tool for designing relational schemas

questions.explanation: Drivers allow the operating system to communicate with hardware devices.

questions.question: A multiple-choice item answered correctly by almost every student may have limited ability to:

options.text: Distinguish between students at different achievement levels

questions.explanation: An item with very high facility may offer little discrimination, though it can still test essential knowledge.

questions.question: Clustering is typically used to:

options.text: Group examples by similarity without predefined class labels
Predict a known numeric target using labeled examples only
Translate every source file into machine code
Encrypt a message with a public key

questions.explanation: Clustering discovers groups in unlabeled data.

questions.question: For a two-input XOR gate, output is 1 when:
questions.explanation: XOR produces 1 for unequal input values.

questions.question: A learner repeatedly confuses two related concepts. A useful first step is to:

options.text: Ask diagnostic questions to locate the misconception
Avoid the concepts for the rest of the year
Give the same explanation repeatedly without checking

questions.explanation: Diagnostic questioning identifies the source of confusion so instruction can target it.

questions.question: Which storage medium has no moving mechanical parts and uses flash memory?
questions.explanation: Solid-state drives use flash memory and have no spinning platters.

questions.question: A 3-to-8 decoder has how many output lines?
questions.explanation: A decoder with n input bits typically has 2^n output lines.

questions.question: An open-ended question is one that:

options.text: Allows several reasoned responses rather than a single fixed answer
Can only be answered yes or no
Has no connection to the lesson

questions.explanation: Open-ended prompts invite explanation and multiple defensible responses.

questions.question: If a worker completes a job in 6 days at a constant rate, the fraction completed in one day is:
questions.explanation: At a constant rate, one day's work is 1/6 of the job.

questions.question: An item bought for ₹400 is sold for ₹460. The profit percentage is:
TCP congestion control is intended to:

options.text: Adapt the sending rate to network congestion
Guarantee zero packet loss in every network

questions.explanation: TCP adjusts transmission behavior to avoid overwhelming the network.

questions.question: Friction usually acts to:

options.text: Oppose relative motion or the tendency of surfaces to slide

questions.explanation: Friction opposes relative sliding or its tendency between surfaces.

questions.question: If `realloc` fails for a nonzero requested size, the original allocated block:

options.text: Is always resized to one byte

questions.explanation: On failure realloc returns NULL and the original allocation remains valid; use a temporary pointer.

questions.question: Which task is a classification problem?

options.text: Predicting whether an email is spam or not spam
Predicting tomorrow's exact temperature as a real number

questions.explanation: Classification predicts a discrete category or label.

questions.question: WPA2/WPA3 are associated with securing:
questions.explanation: WPA2 and WPA3 are Wi-Fi security protocols.

questions.question: A student portfolio is particularly useful for showing:

options.text: Development and examples of work over time

questions.explanation: Portfolios document progress, reflection and work samples across time.

questions.question: The area of a rectangle of length 9 cm and breadth 4 cm is:
questions.explanation: Area = length × breadth = 9 × 4 = 36 cm².

questions.question: A simple undirected graph with n vertices can have at most how many edges?
questions.explanation: There is at most one edge for each unordered pair of distinct vertices.

questions.question: Compared with separate processes, threads in the same process typically share:

options.text: A separate copy of every memory page in all cases

questions.explanation: Threads share process address space and resources but have their own execution state.

questions.question: When a learner struggles to read small text, the teacher should first:

options.text: Identify the access barrier and provide an appropriate accommodation
Remove the learner from all reading tasks
Give a lower grade before investigating

questions.explanation: Identifying and addressing access needs supports participation.

questions.question: Which is a renewable energy source when naturally replenished?
questions.explanation: Solar energy is replenished by ongoing sunlight, unlike fossil fuels.

questions.question: Which is the largest Indian state by area?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan is India's largest state by area.

questions.question: Regular expressions in formal-language theory describe:
questions.explanation: Classical regular expressions characterize regular languages.

questions.question: Which address is a private IPv4 address?
questions.explanation: 172.16.0.0/12 is a private range, which includes 172.20.10.5.

questions.question: A /26 IPv4 subnet contains how many total addresses?
questions.explanation: There are 32−26=6 host bits, so 2^6 = 64 total addresses.

questions.question: A leaf node is a node that has:
questions.explanation: A leaf has degree zero in the rooted-tree child relationship.

questions.question: If X→Y, the dependency states that:

options.text: Each X value determines a single Y value in the relation
X and Y must be candidate keys
X and Y cannot share attributes

questions.explanation: A functional dependency constrains tuples with equal X values to have equal Y values.

questions.question: External fragmentation occurs when:

options.text: Free memory is split into noncontiguous holes
Every allocated block contains no internal waste
All memory is used by one process

questions.explanation: Total free memory may be sufficient but scattered among small holes.

questions.question: A deque allows insertion and deletion:
questions.explanation: A double-ended queue supports operations at both ends.

questions.question: Captions on instructional videos primarily support:

options.text: Access to spoken content for deaf or hard-of-hearing learners and other viewers

questions.explanation: Captions provide a text representation of speech and relevant audio cues.

questions.question: A fuse is designed to:

options.text: Break a circuit when excessive current flows
Store electrical energy like a battery

questions.explanation: A fuse melts under excessive current to interrupt the circuit.

questions.question: The '3Rs' in waste management stand for:
questions.explanation: The 3Rs prioritize reducing waste, reusing items and recycling materials.

questions.question: In Python, `dict.get(key)` returns None by default when:

options.text: The key is absent and no default is supplied
The key is present with any value

questions.explanation: get avoids KeyError for missing keys and defaults to None unless another default is supplied.

questions.question: Choose the next letter: B, E, H, K, __.
questions.explanation: The sequence advances three letters each time: B, E, H, K, N.

questions.question: A version-control commit typically records:

options.text: A snapshot or change set in project history

questions.explanation: Commits preserve project changes and metadata in repository history.

questions.question: Thorndike's law of effect suggests that responses followed by satisfying consequences are more likely to:
questions.explanation: The law of effect links satisfying consequences with strengthened response tendencies.

questions.question: Dynamic method dispatch selects an overridden method based on:
questions.explanation: Runtime polymorphism resolves an overridden instance method using the object's dynamic type.

questions.question: If the objective is to perform a practical computer task, the strongest assessment is usually:

options.text: A performance task with observable criteria
A spelling test unrelated to the task
A survey about favourite subjects only

questions.explanation: Performance objectives are best assessed by observing performance against criteria.

questions.question: Firmware is best described as:

options.text: Application software installed by the user
Low-level software stored in non-volatile memory to control hardware
A temporary file created by an editor
A network protocol for file transfer

questions.explanation: Firmware provides low-level control and is commonly stored in flash or other non-volatile memory.

questions.question: A half adder produces:

options.text: Sum and carry from two input bits
Sum, carry-in and carry-out from three inputs
A stored bit with a clock

questions.explanation: A half adder adds two bits and outputs sum and carry.

questions.question: A relation is in BCNF when for every non-trivial functional dependency X→Y, X is:
questions.explanation: BCNF requires every determinant of a non-trivial FD to be a superkey.

questions.question: An incremental backup typically copies:

options.text: Data changed since the most recent backup of any type
Only files that have never changed

questions.explanation: Incremental backups record changes since the last backup, reducing backup size.

questions.question: When using a shared computer, a learner should:

options.text: Sign out of accounts and avoid saving credentials on the device
Leave all accounts logged in for convenience
Share browser passwords with the next user

questions.explanation: Signing out and not saving credentials helps protect accounts on shared devices.

questions.question: Disjoint-set union structures are commonly used to:

options.text: Track connected components while processing edges

questions.explanation: Union-find efficiently supports merging sets and checking whether elements share a set.

questions.question: Which statement about `sizeof` is generally correct?

options.text: It returns the size in bytes of an object or type
It always returns the number of array elements
It evaluates every operand at runtime

questions.explanation: sizeof yields a size in bytes and its result type is size_t; some operands are unevaluated.

questions.question: The Earth's rotation is primarily responsible for:

options.text: The cycle of day and night
The annual change in Earth's distance from the Sun only

questions.explanation: Earth's rotation causes different regions to face toward and away from the Sun.

questions.question: A constructor is primarily used to:

options.text: Return a value of any type

questions.explanation: Constructors establish an object's initial state.

questions.question: HTTP status code 404 generally means:
questions.explanation: 404 indicates the requested resource was not found.

questions.question: A person faces east, turns left, then turns left again. Which direction are they facing?
questions.explanation: Facing east, left gives north; another left gives west.

questions.question: A decision problem is decidable if there exists an algorithm that:

options.text: Halts on every input and answers correctly
Halts only when the answer is yes
Works only on finite input lengths fixed in advance

questions.explanation: Decidability requires a terminating correct procedure for all valid inputs.

questions.question: After a minor conflict, a restorative conversation focuses on:

options.text: Impact, responsibility and steps to repair harm
Finding a student to shame publicly

questions.explanation: Restorative approaches help learners understand impact and repair relationships.

questions.question: An admissible heuristic for A* never:

options.text: Overestimates the true minimum remaining cost

questions.explanation: Admissibility means the heuristic estimate is no greater than the true optimal remaining cost.

questions.question: An opcode specifies:

options.text: The IP address of the host
The number of users logged in

questions.explanation: The opcode identifies the instruction's operation.

questions.question: Which protocol is commonly used by a mail client to submit outgoing email to a mail server?
questions.explanation: SMTP is used for sending/submitting email; POP3 and IMAP are used to access mailboxes.

questions.question: A critical section is the part of a program that:

options.text: Accesses shared resources requiring controlled concurrent access
Runs only before the OS boots

questions.explanation: Mutual exclusion or other synchronization protects shared state in a critical section.

questions.question: Peer tutoring works best when:

options.text: Roles, tasks and support expectations are clear to both learners
The tutor is expected to replace the teacher completely
The learner receiving help is publicly labelled as weak

questions.explanation: Structure helps peer support remain respectful, focused and effective.

questions.question: A school timetable should primarily balance:

options.text: Curricular requirements, available resources and learner needs
Only the personal preference of one teacher
Only the number of classroom doors

questions.explanation: Timetabling coordinates learning needs, staff, rooms and subject requirements.

questions.question: A vectored interrupt system provides:

options.text: A way to identify the interrupt service routine location
A guarantee that interrupts never overlap
A separate CPU for each device
Automatic conversion of interrupts to polling

questions.explanation: The interrupt vector identifies or points to the appropriate service routine.

questions.question: In a little-endian system, the least significant byte is stored at the:

options.text: Lowest memory address of a multi-byte value
Highest memory address of every value
Same address as all other bytes

questions.explanation: Little-endian stores the least significant byte at the lowest address.

questions.question: Every regular language is also:
questions.explanation: Regular languages form a subset of context-free languages.

questions.question: A type checker primarily detects errors such as:

options.text: Incompatible operations or assignments between types

questions.explanation: Type checking validates compatibility according to language type rules.

questions.question: Containers differ from traditional virtual machines because containers typically:

options.text: Require a separate guest kernel for each container

questions.explanation: Containers package applications while sharing the host kernel, unlike full guest OS VMs.

questions.question: An Ethernet switch learns forwarding information primarily from the:

options.text: Source MAC address of incoming frames
Destination IP address of every packet only

questions.explanation: Switches learn which source MAC addresses are reachable on which ports.

questions.question: In REST-style APIs, a resource is commonly identified by a:
questions.explanation: URIs identify resources in web architectures.

questions.question: A is the mother of B. B is the brother of C. How is A related to C?
questions.explanation: B and C are siblings, so A is C's mother as well.

questions.question: An AVL tree maintains a balance factor at each node typically in:
questions.explanation: The height difference between left and right subtrees is at most one.

questions.question: A teacher explains a rule and then asks learners to apply it to several cases. This is mainly:
questions.explanation: Deduction starts with a principle and applies it to particular cases.

questions.question: The POST routine is generally used to:
questions.explanation: Power-On Self-Test checks basic hardware functionality during startup.

questions.question: A diagnostic test is especially useful for:

options.text: Identifying specific strengths, misconceptions or learning gaps before targeted support

questions.explanation: Diagnostic assessment informs the nature of subsequent instruction or intervention.

questions.question: Plagiarism is best described as:

options.text: Presenting another person's work or ideas as one's own without proper acknowledgement

questions.explanation: Plagiarism misrepresents the source or ownership of work.

questions.question: Which classroom action best reflects learner-centred teaching?

options.text: Learners investigate a problem and explain their reasoning while the teacher facilitates
The teacher speaks for the entire period and students copy notes
Every learner completes the same task without feedback
The textbook is read aloud without discussion

questions.explanation: Learner-centred instruction actively engages students in constructing and explaining understanding.

questions.question: In an inductive approach, learners generally move from:

options.text: Specific examples to a general rule
A general rule to a worked example only

questions.explanation: Induction builds a generalization from observed instances.

questions.question: Multi-factor authentication requires:

options.text: Two or more distinct categories of evidence
Two passwords from the same category only
A public website and a private website

questions.explanation: Factors commonly include something known, possessed, or inherent.

questions.question: A TLS certificate is used in part to:

options.text: Bind a public key to an identity under a certificate authority's signature
Store the user's password in readable form
Guarantee a site contains no malicious content

questions.explanation: Certificates support identity authentication by associating a public key with a named subject.

questions.question: Scaffolding is best described as:

options.text: Temporary support that is gradually reduced as competence grows
Permanent completion of every task by the teacher
A form of grading based only on rank

questions.explanation: Scaffolding provides support matched to current need and fades as independence develops.

questions.question: Who was the first President of the Republic of India?
questions.explanation: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was India's first President.

questions.question: A pushdown automaton differs from a finite automaton mainly because it has:

options.text: An unbounded number of control states for every input

questions.explanation: A stack gives a PDA memory useful for recognizing context-free languages.

questions.question: Metacognition refers to a learner's ability to:

options.text: Plan, monitor and evaluate their own thinking or learning

questions.explanation: Metacognition is awareness and regulation of one's cognitive processes.

questions.question: When evaluating a website's credibility, which check is most useful?

options.text: Author expertise, evidence, date and corroboration
Whether the headline agrees with one's opinion

questions.explanation: Credibility depends on authorship, evidence, currency and independent confirmation.

questions.question: Which property defines a stable sorting algorithm?

options.text: Equal-key elements retain their relative order
The algorithm always runs in O(n log n)
The algorithm uses no auxiliary memory

questions.explanation: Stability preserves original relative order among equal-key records.

questions.question: Composition models a relationship most closely described as:

options.text: Has-a, with lifecycle ownership often stronger than simple association

questions.explanation: Composition represents an object built from or owning other objects.

questions.question: Horizontal scaling generally means:

options.text: Increasing RAM in one existing machine only

questions.explanation: Horizontal scaling adds nodes or instances to share load.

questions.question: To improve fairness in an assessment, a teacher should:

options.text: Use criteria aligned with the stated objectives and apply them consistently
Change the marking rule for each student without reason
Assess handwriting when the objective is programming logic

questions.explanation: Consistent, relevant criteria make assessment more equitable and valid.

questions.question: A function pointer can be used to:

options.text: Store the address of a function and call it indirectly
Store a whole function's machine code in an int portably
Change a function's return type at runtime

questions.explanation: Function pointers allow indirect calls through a compatible function address.

questions.question: In a food chain, producers are organisms that:

options.text: Make organic food from inorganic substances using energy
Obtain all energy by eating animals
Always occupy the highest trophic level

questions.explanation: Plants and some other organisms produce organic matter, often using sunlight.

questions.question: In JavaScript, `===` differs from `==` because `===`:

options.text: Does not perform type coercion for equality comparison

questions.explanation: Strict equality compares without coercing operand types.

questions.question: For 8-bit signed two's-complement representation, the minimum value is:
questions.explanation: The range is −2^7 through 2^7−1, or −128 to 127.

questions.question: Which flip-flop toggles its output when its T input is 1 at the active clock edge?
questions.explanation: A T flip-flop toggles when T=1.

questions.question: What is the effect of `typedef` in C?

options.text: It creates a new distinct runtime type in every case
It introduces an alias for a type name
It allocates storage for an object
It converts a structure to a union

questions.explanation: typedef provides an alternative name for an existing type.

questions.question: In an LR parser, a shift-reduce conflict means the parser cannot decide whether to:

options.text: Shift the next input symbol or reduce by a production
Allocate heap memory or release it
Open or close a network port

questions.explanation: The parsing table contains competing shift and reduce actions for a state/input pair.

questions.question: Abstraction in OOP focuses on:

options.text: Essential features while hiding unnecessary implementation detail
Copying objects byte by byte only

questions.explanation: Abstraction exposes relevant behavior while hiding internal complexity.

questions.question: In a doubly linked list, each ordinary node typically stores:

options.text: Only a data field and no links
Data plus next and previous links
A left and right child only
A hash function and bucket number

questions.explanation: Doubly linked nodes maintain links in both directions.

questions.question: The Program Counter normally contains:

options.text: The address associated with the next instruction to fetch
The address of the top of every process stack

questions.explanation: The PC tracks the next instruction address, subject to architecture-specific details.

questions.question: Network Address Translation is commonly used to:

options.text: Map private addresses to public addresses or other address mappings

questions.explanation: NAT rewrites address information, commonly enabling private hosts to share public IPv4 addresses.

questions.question: What does `const int *p` indicate?

options.text: The pointed-to int cannot be modified through p
Both p and the pointed-to int are always constant

questions.explanation: It is a pointer to const int; the pointer itself may be reassigned.

questions.question: An intermediate representation is useful because it:

options.text: Separates source-language details from target-specific code generation
Removes the need to parse source code
Guarantees every program is optimized perfectly

questions.explanation: IR supports analysis and optimization across source and target choices.

questions.question: In UTF-8, a Unicode code point may be represented using:
questions.explanation: UTF-8 uses variable-length sequences of one to four bytes.

questions.question: A write-ahead log requires that relevant log records be written to stable storage:

options.text: After all data pages are always written
Before the corresponding modified data pages are written
Only after the database is shut down
Only when a query returns zero rows

questions.explanation: WAL ensures recovery information is durable before corresponding data-page writes.

questions.question: A budget deficit occurs when, over the relevant period:

options.text: Expenditure exceeds receipts under the stated deficit measure

questions.explanation: A deficit measures a shortfall between specified expenditure and receipts.

questions.question: Function points estimate software size primarily from:
questions.explanation: Function-point analysis estimates functional size from user-facing capabilities.

questions.question: Which nutrient is the body's main readily available energy source?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are a major source of energy in the diet.

questions.question: A model with high bias is often characterized by:
questions.explanation: High bias reflects overly restrictive assumptions and can cause underfitting.

questions.question: A dirty read occurs when a transaction reads:

options.text: Data written by another transaction that has not committed
Only data from a committed snapshot
A row with no primary key

questions.explanation: Uncommitted changes may later be rolled back, making the read dirty.

questions.question: A well-designed module generally aims for:

options.text: High cohesion and high coupling always
No interfaces between modules under any conditions

questions.explanation: Modules should have focused responsibilities and limited dependencies.

questions.question: Classical conditioning involves learning an association between:

options.text: A reward and a voluntary response only

questions.explanation: Classical conditioning forms associations between stimuli.

questions.question: Dynamic programming is especially useful when a problem has:

options.text: No repeated states and no structure
A requirement to avoid storing results

questions.explanation: Memoization or tabulation reuses subproblem results.

questions.question: A cryptographic hash function is designed to map input data to:

options.text: A reversible ciphertext with a universal key
A guaranteed unique identifier for every possible input

questions.explanation: Hashes produce fixed-size digests; collisions are possible and preimages are intended to be hard to find.

questions.question: Classroom rules are most effective when they are:

options.text: Clear, few in number, taught and applied consistently
Applied only to students who ask questions
Kept secret until a violation occurs
